validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: could not corroborate. Searched WebSearch in both Russian ('Ачинск Абакан газопровод', 'газопровод Ачинск-Абакан Газпром') and English ('Achinsk-Abakan gas pipeline'); zero hits beyond GEM's own wiki page and pages that appear to mirror/cite GEM. Read GEM's own wiki citation list for this PID (per standing rule, for leads only, never as a citation) -- none of its listed sources name this specific route either. Downloaded and full-text-searched the archived (Wayback, 2020-10-07 snapshot) Gazprom corporate Power-of-Siberia/Krasnoyarsk-gasification project page -- zero occurrences of 'Achinsk' or 'Abakan' (Cyrillic or Latin) anywhere in the page text. Also checked newslab.ru coverage of the Proskokovo-Achinsk-Krasnoyarsk-Kansk-Balagansk scheme (the real, confirmed P2376 route, which DOES pass through Achinsk) -- that scheme terminates east at Balagansk (Irkutsk Oblast), never south to Abakan; no source treats 'Achinsk-Abakan' as a spur or alternate branch of it. CLASSIFICATION: cannot assess -- no document to classify. REVIVAL CHECK: per the batch's own guidance to check P2376/P2703/P6535 for a Krasnoyarsk-gasification or Power-of-Siberia-2 revival -- found none; the Oct 2024 Krasnoyarsk gasification roadmap (Kotyukov/Miller, tvknews.ru) relies on autonomous LNG/propane-butane gasification, not any new trunk pipeline, and Power-of-Siberia-2 discourse (Kommersant 2022-09-01) is an east-west export corridor near these cities, never described as reaching Abakan. Both real endpoint cities exist (Achinsk, Krasnoyarsk Krai; Abakan, Republic of Khakassia) and are ~300 km apart, which may be the origin of a plausible-sounding but unsubstantiated entry. Recommend this row be flagged for existence review rather than researched further under the current sourcing base -- exhaustive search performed.
